clauses.reason: Section 1 closes all executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government on January 9, 2025 ("shall be closed on January 9, 2025, as a mark of respect for James Earl"). The text gives the reason as a mark of respect for James Earl Carter, Jr., the thirty-ninth President of the United States; it does not excuse employees from duty in section 1, which only closes the departments and agencies. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on January 9, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past January 9, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-01-09, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when January 9, 2025 begins.

Section 2 lets the heads of departments and agencies decide that certain offices and installations must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on the closed day, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public need ("must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on"). It is a discretion that attaches to the closure in section 1 and has no operation once the closed day is over. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on January 9, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past January 9, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-01-09, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when January 9, 2025 begins.

Section 3 provides that the closed day shall be considered as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and leave of employees ("January 9, 2025, shall be considered as falling within the scope"). It is a deeming rule for the closed day only. Executive Order 11582 is an earlier order cited as the pay-and-leave framework; it is not a later event and does not end this order. The pay and leave consequences for the closed day are recorded under savings. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on January 9, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past January 9, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-01-09, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when January 9, 2025 begins.

Section 4 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to take such actions as may be necessary to implement the order ("such actions as may be necessary to implement this order."). It is an implementation command with no stated date and no held record of what the Director did or when. It implements only the closure of the departments and agencies on January 9, 2025 (section 1) and the provisions attached to that closed day (sections 2 and 3), so it is read as having no operation after January 9, 2025; that reading is an inference from the order's text and is disclosed, and it does not rest on any completion date. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on January 9, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past January 9, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-01-09, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when January 9, 2025 begins.

It is a rule of construction attached to the order's operative sections and ends with them. It is a rule of construction, not a command, and ends with the order's operative sections. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on January 9, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past January 9, 2025. It is a rule of construction, not a command, and ends with the order's operative sections. This general provision says the order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. It is a condition on how the sections are carried out, not a separate command, and it has nothing to condition once the sections have ended. It is a statement about the order's effect, not a command, and ends with the order's operative sections. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 14133, 90 FR 187 (Federal Register Vol. 90, No. 2, Friday, January 3, 2025; filed January 2, 2025), signed December 30, 2024 (grade official_original_counted, machine text layer of the official PDF). The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on January 9, 2025) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), with no separate lead clause; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on January 9, 2025 and says nothing that runs past January 9, 2025, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2025-01-09. No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.

savings.reason: Savings: the order contains no savings or continuing-effects wording other than its rules of construction. The pay and leave consequences of the closed day under section 3 (Executive Order 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b)) are accrued consequences governed by those authorities, not commands of this order; the held sources show no open claim.
